clinicalPearls: Umbrella term for autosomal recessive demyelinating CMT, with subtypes defined by causative genes such as GDAP1, MTMR2, SBF2, SH3TC2, NDRG1, EGR2 and PRX
Tends to present in early childhood with severe, rapidly progressive weakness, delayed motor milestones and often loss of ambulation earlier than dominant CMT1
Recessive inheritance means parents are usually unaffected and consanguinity increases the risk, so a negative family history should not exclude the diagnosis
Nerve conduction studies show markedly slowed motor conduction velocities consistent with a diffuse demyelinating process
Subtype-specific features occur, including early scoliosis (SH3TC2), deafness and gait ataxia (NDRG1, Lom type), vocal cord and diaphragmatic weakness (GDAP1) and prominent sensory ataxia (PRX)
Sural nerve biopsy may show distinctive findings such as focally folded myelin (MTMR2/SBF2) that help subtype classification
Diagnosis relies on the recessive pattern, demyelinating electrophysiology and gene panel confirmation
reference.pathophysiology: CMT4 comprises several autosomal recessive demyelinating neuropathies in which biallelic loss-of-function variants disrupt Schwann cell proteins essential for myelin formation and maintenance. The affected genes influence diverse pathways, including mitochondrial and membrane dynamics (GDAP1), endosomal phosphoinositide regulation (MTMR2, SBF2), Schwann cell signalling and myelin protein trafficking (SH3TC2), and myelin structural integrity (PRX, EGR2, NDRG1). Failure of these processes causes defective myelination, segmental demyelination and remyelination with onion-bulb formation, and eventual secondary axonal loss. Because myelination is broadly impaired, motor conduction velocities are uniformly and severely slowed.
additionalDifferentials: Metachromatic leukodystrophy and other leukodystrophies with neuropathy
Refsum disease and other metabolic neuropathies
additionalInvestigations: Nerve conduction studies demonstrating severe uniform slowing
Autosomal recessive CMT gene panel or exome sequencing
Sural nerve biopsy in selected cases to identify subtype-specific myelin changes
Spinal imaging and orthopaedic review for early scoliosis
Audiometry where sensorineural deafness is suspected
Respiratory and vocal cord assessment in GDAP1-related disease
redFlags: Early respiratory or diaphragmatic weakness causing breathing difficulty
Rapidly progressive weakness with loss of ambulation in childhood
Superimposed subacute deterioration suggesting an acquired inflammatory neuropathy
reference.prognosis: Generally more severe than dominant CMT, with many children losing independent walking by adolescence; however, severity varies by subtype and specific variant. Respiratory involvement in some forms can affect life expectancy.
pitfalls: Excluding CMT because the family history is negative in a recessive disorder
Failing to screen for scoliosis, deafness or respiratory involvement associated with particular subtypes
Missing a treatable acquired demyelinating neuropathy in a child
Not offering genetic counselling and carrier testing to consanguineous families
references: Bradley and Daroff's Neurology in Clinical Practice
management: No disease-modifying drug exists, so structured physiotherapy and occupational therapy to preserve strength, joint range and function, with stretching to prevent contractures, form the mainstay
Ankle-foot orthoses, orthopaedic footwear and mobility aids to support foot drop and maintain safe gait for as long as possible
Orthopaedic review with bracing or corrective surgery for progressive foot deformity and for early scoliosis, notably in SH3TC2-related disease
Respiratory surveillance with non-invasive ventilation, and vocal-cord assessment, in subtypes with diaphragmatic or laryngeal weakness such as GDAP1-related disease
Periodic audiometry for sensorineural deafness in NDRG1 (Lom) type and monitoring of ambulation and spinal alignment
Avoid neurotoxic drugs such as vincristine that can accelerate the neuropathy
Coordinated neuromuscular multidisciplinary care including podiatry, orthotics and rehabilitation medicine
Genetic counselling and family screening given autosomal recessive inheritance, with attention to consanguinity
